prs.body:
@mDuo13 identified a potential issue if amendments go live in an unexpected order.  Suppose the Checks amendment were to go live before fix1623.  Then, later, fix1623 goes live.  If that occurred, a CheckCash that specified `DeliverMin` in the pre-fix1623 window could return a synthetic `delivered_amount` of "0" after fix1623 went live.  Not correct.  A better response would be "unavailable".

Although we don't expect amendments to go live in the wrong order, this fix is still correct and might be useful if future transaction types start returning the synthetic `delivered_amount` field.

This change is not on an amendment, since it does not affect any data that goes in the ledger.  It only affects the value returned in a synthetic field in the metadata.

Reviewers: @mDuo13 @miguelportilla.

comments.author: scottschurr
comments.body: @intelliot, Changing the amendment name would certainly be the most secure thing to do.  However there have been previous amendments that have been published to the network but not completely finished until a later release.  At the moment I think `Checks` is following that example.  Not to say that we couldn't tighten up our process.  But I'd like input from @nbougalis before we choose to do that.

comments.author: nbougalis
comments.body:
Re: amendment name... the amendment hasn’t yet been activated and this PR corrects a technical flaw in the original implementation. Under these circumstances, I don’t think it’s necessary to change the name.

Is the concern here that someone will be running 0.90 after we release 1.0 with a fix and have issues?

One could make that argument, but if that’s the case, then a `fix` amendment for this seems more appropriate and we simply propose activating the fix first and `Checks` later. But now we’re adding two amendments...

comments.author: intelliot
comments.body:
Exactly - there will likely be rippled servers running 0.90 on the network. Don't we want them to be amendment blocked if they don't have this fix?

If we want it to be one amendment, we could rename it. `ChecksV2` or `Checks1.0.1` for example.

comments.author: scottschurr
comments.body: Not that we can rely on this in all cases, but in the specific 1.0.0 case there's a different amendment (`fix1543`) which, assuming it goes live with 1.0.0, would amendment block any nodes running 0.90.0.  Here's the commit: https://github.com/ripple/rippled/commit/d45556ec823ae896f35e671f269f8612330a836d#diff-9b4c07353136ece3af67c68aca12ff63R363.  That commit was added in 1.0.0-b4.

comments.author: intelliot
comments.body: I _think_ there will be no problems if `fix1543` is activated before `Checks`.

comments.author: scottschurr
comments.body:
Another consideration is that, regarding ledger health, it's really only important that the _validators_ are on 1.0.0 when the `Checks` amendment goes live.  Leaving `fix1543` out of consideration, if a non-validator node is running 0.90.0 when `Checks` goes live, then that node will see a disagreement between the ledger it built and the one accepted by the network.  So that node will see more frequent de-syncs.  It's less explicit than being amendment blocked, but the problem is limited to those non-validator nodes that are running 0.90.0.

The story changes dramatically if there are validator nodes running 0.90.0.  But, at least for the time being, that's less of a concern.

comments.author: mDuo13
comments.body:
If we're changing the behavior of an amendment from a released version, we should change its name and ID. Full stop.

The point of the Amendments system is to make it clear when people aren't running the rules agreed by a consensus of the network. That includes this case. Changing the amendment's functionality (even just a little bit) but not its name/ID is almost as bad as not having an amendment at all.

Just because there happen to be circumstances around this one (like a separate fix amendment that's likely to go live first/at the same time, essentially doing the job of amendment blocking servers for this one) doesn't make it a good practice. What if the other fix amendment doesn't get approved for some reason? What about alternate ledger chains that already have Checks enabled?

Let's just change it to Checksv2, please.

comments.author: scottschurr
comments.body:
@mDuo13 and @intelliot:  @nbougalis and I have talked this over.  My current intention is to add a `fix` that enabled just this change for `delivered_amount`.  We will enable that `fix` on the network before enabling the `Checks` amendment.  Objections?

For the longer term we probably need to rethink how we've been handling amendments with an eye toward broader control of validators.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Excellent question, @mDuo13.  This specific topic came up when I was talking with Dave Cohen in San Francisco last December.  Dave's position was that all transactions that transfer funds (including all `Payment` transactions, not just the partials) should put their final outcome in a `delivered_amount` field.  This would have the potential to vastly simplify the computational hoops that an exchange has to jump through.

If we can simplify the life of an exchange I'm all for it.  However we need to think hard about some transactions like `EscrowCreate`.  From an _exchange's_ perspective does that XRP still belong to the owning account, even though the XRP is, for now, locked away in the `Escrow`?  I think we'd want to be _really_ clear about the information we intend to convey before we make a change of this nature.

FWIW, since the `delivered_amount` is synthesized, we could make this change at any time without an Amendment.  I just want to make sure we've thought it through really carefully (and consulted an expert on exchanges) before we make the change.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
I've attempted to resolve a couple of these nits with a `[FOLD]` commit.  But I'll add a couple of comments:

1. My inclination is to brace initialize whenever it's reasonable.  When general brace initialization was introduced in C++11, the goal was that everyone could use it everywhere.  And it would be safer that other forms of initialization since it doesn't narrow.  That failed.  Anything with an `initializer_list` constructor (like `vector`) causes problems.  `auto` causes problems (although we hope that improves with C++17).  But in my effort to think as little as possible while coding I reach for `{}` initialization by default unless I know of a reason not to.  Effective Modern C++ Item 7 is my basic guide here.

2. In this particular lambda, the passed parameter is a member of the class, not a local.  I can't capture that.  I can capture `this`, but that passes more information to the lambda that the lambda requires.  So I chose to solve the problem by passing just the member variable that I needed as a parameter.

Hope that helps.

The `[FOLD]` commit resolves nits 2 and 3 by replacing the lambda with a ternary operator (as @HowardHinnant mentioned might be a choice).
